To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
PGA-coated cationic liposomes of siRNA-Chols were effective for siRNA delivery to the liver and the suppression of gene expressions in vivo.
PGA-coated liposomes of siRNA-Chols are a promising vector of siRNA for targeting the liver.
PGA-coated liposomes are a promising delivery system for siRNA targeting to the liver.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a systemic siRNA delivery system by intravenous injection.
the development of a new siRNA delivery system to the liver by PGA coatings for cationsic lipoplex.
the development of a novel anionic polymer-coating system for cationic-liposome/siRNA lipoplexes to improve the stability and targeting to the liver.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the anionic polymers, CS and PAA, are useful to prevent the agglutinability of lipoplexes with blood components and to increase the association between cationic liposomes and siRNA, while the anionic polymer, PGA, might be a useful coating polymer for cationic-liposome/siRNA complex to produce a systemic vector to the liver.
PGA-coated cationic liposomes are a promising carrier for siRNA targeting the liver.
PGA-coated liposome of siRNA-Cholestryl ether is an effective and non-toxic vector for in vivo siRNA delivery to the liver.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
PGA-coated liposomes are useful for the systemic delivery of siRNA to liver.
the anionic polymer coatings for cation lipoplex of cholesterol-modified siRNAs can be a useful strategy for the development of a vector of siRNA for systemic gene silencing.
the PGA-coated liposome is an attractive vector for siRNA delivery to the liver by intravenous injection.
The main takeaway from our work is that

PGA coating for cationic siRNA-liposome complexes is useful to achieve the systemic delivery of siRNA for gene silencing in vivo, although the mechanism of gene silencing by PGA-coated liposome is not clear.
the PGA coating of lipoplexes can deliver siRNA to the livers of mice by intravenous injection.
the use of cholesterol-conjugated siRNAs with anionic polymer-coatings can be used as an effective siRNA delivery system.
